title: Photo‐ thermal isomerization and degradation of β‐carotene in a model beverage system under varying pH and oxygen conditions and corresponding protective strategies
content:
Abstract

Background

Photo-thermal stability is a critical indicator of the quality of food products containing β-carotene. The differences in the degradation mechanisms of emulsified β-carotene in beverage matrices under different light and thermal conditions, as well as the effects of environmental factors such as pH and oxygen partial pressure, require systematic investigation to develop effective stabilization strategies.

Results

Accelerated light exposure experiments revealed that cis-β-carotene first underwent photo-isomerization to all-trans-β-carotene. This was followed by overall degradation, suggesting that cis-to-trans isomerization might be favored at high cis-isomer ratios. Compared with pH 3.0, pH 6.0 markedly enhanced both photo-stability and thermal stability of cis-β-carotene and all-trans-β-carotene by suppressing protonation-triggered initiation. Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spin trapping confirmed that acid (H+) promoted the formation of free radicals, which rapidly accelerated β-carotene degradation. Oxygen partial pressure significantly accelerated the photo-degradation of 13-cis-β-carotene and the thermal degradation of 9-cis-β-carotene, whereas all-trans-β-carotene demonstrated the highest stability. The addition of ascorbic acid and water-soluble rosemary extract effectively enhanced the photo-thermal stability of β-carotene in beverages, extending its shelf life to 20 weeks (under 24 h illumination).

Conclusion

This study provides insights into the degradation mechanisms of β-carotene emulsions in beverages. The stability of β-carotene was governed both by structural characteristics and environmental factors. All-trans-β-carotene remained dominant across all conditions due to its stable conformation. The pH value and oxygen partial pressure were identified as critical factors influencing stability. These results provide strategies for selecting antioxidant combinations to develop more stable β-carotene-fortified beverages with extended shelf life. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.
